upstream_preparation_contexts.label: Solvent and reagent conditioning
upstream_preparation_contexts.details: Hydrocarbon solvents and alcohols were dried over unspecified standard desiccants and stored over molecular sieves. GdCl3(Aldrich) was vacuum-dried at110°C/10^-2torr and checked for chlorine content; drying duration is unreported.

upstream_preparation_contexts.label: Gadolinium tert-butoxide
upstream_preparation_contexts.details: [Gd3(OBut)9(ButOH)2] is prepared from [Gd{N(SiMe3)2}3] and tert-butanol, referencing46. Quantities and reaction schedule are absent. The heterometallic route instead explicitly generates Gd isopropoxide in situ; the tert-butoxide context is not forced into that route.

upstream_preparation_contexts.label: Iron tert-butoxide
upstream_preparation_contexts.details: [Fe2(OBut)6] is prepared by salt elimination between FeCl3 and3equivalents NaOBut in THF/toluene, citing47. Absolute charges, solvent ratio, temperature, duration and isolation details are absent.

characterization_methods.precursor_XRD: Crystal sealed in inert atmosphere in Lindemann capillary; SiemensSmart CCD, MoKalpha0.71073angstrom;25centeredreflections, Lorentz/polarization and semiempirical absorption corrections; SHELXS86/SHELXL97, H atoms riding on carbon.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3–5, Experimental and XPS discussion

source_interpretation.text: The authors use a heterometallic alkoxide with Gd/Fe = 1:1 and existing Gd–O–Fe connections. They argue that atomic-scale cation mixing avoids the intermediate phases possible when separate metal salts are mixed. This is source-attributed synthesis reasoning, not an independently verified reaction mechanism.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, 4, Introduction, molecular precursor and conclusion

source_interpretation.text: Water activation creates a sol and gel. The authors attribute the thermal-loss stages to solvent loss, removal of alkoxy groups, then dehydroxylation/condensation. A DTA exotherm around 680 °C accompanies oxide crystallization; it is an analytical signal, not an additional synthesis dwell.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2, 5, Thermal discussion and Nanopowder Synthesis

source_interpretation.text: The 600 °C powder is amorphous, 700 °C shows initial crystallization and 800 °C shows a developed orthoferrite pattern. The 45, 55 and 70 nm values are XRD crystallite estimates at 800, 1000 and 1200 °C. The approximately 60 nm faceted crystallites in TEM belong specifically to the 1000 °C specimen.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 2–3 and structural discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Phase purity has a defined evidence scope
source_interpretation.text: The diffraction discussion reports no garnet or other crystalline intermediate, and EDX reports no cation segregation at examined spots. These observations do not establish every possible impurity below detection or provide measured atomic coordinates. The molecular precursor cell in Table 1 must not be used as the oxide cell.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, 5, XRD/EDX discussion and Table 1

source_interpretation.text: The authors interpret the near-linear response as a dominant Gd paramagnetic contribution plus weak ferromagnetism from canting in the Fe sublattice. Their series-level coercivity and model-derived canting values are retained as context, not assigned as separate precise measurements to both calcination specimens. They report no superparamagnetic response in the examined size range.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure 4 and magnetic interpretation
